Here’s the concise, precise explanation.

1. Setup and violation
- We insert a new node x as red.
- The only possible violation is: x’s parent p is red (two consecutive reds).
- We must restore the red-black properties without changing the black height of any path.

2. Uncle is red: recolor case
- Let g be p’s parent (grandparent of x).
- If g’s other child (the uncle u) is red:
  - Recolor:
    - p → black
    - u → black
    - g → red
  - Then treat g as the new “problem node” and continue upward.
- Why black height is preserved:
  - Before: paths through g had black height bh(g).
  - After: p and u are black, g is red.
    - Any path from g down to a leaf now has one extra black node (p or u) but one fewer black node (g is no longer black).
    - Net black count on every path through g is unchanged.
  - The red violation (if any) is pushed up to g, so we continue.

3. Uncle is black: triangle rotation case
- Assume u is black (or absent).
- If p and x are on opposite sides of g (e.g., p is left child of g, x is right child of p), we have a “zig-zag” (triangle) shape.
- Perform:
  - A rotation at p in the direction of x (e.g., right-rotate at p if x is p’s right child).
- Effect:
  - x becomes the child of g on the same side as p was.
  - p becomes x’s child.
- Why black height is preserved:

Here’s the concise, precise explanation.

1. Setup and violation
- We insert a new node x as red.
- The only possible violation is: x’s parent p is red (two consecutive reds).
- We must restore the red-black properties without changing the black height of any subtree.

2. Uncle is red: recolor case
- Let g be p’s parent (grandparent of x).
- If g’s other child (the uncle u) is red:
  - Recolor:
    - p → black
    - u → black
    - g → red
  - Then treat g as the new “problem node” and continue upward.
- Why black height is preserved:
  - Before: g was black; both p and u were red.
  - After: g is red; both p and u are black.
  - For any path through g:
    - Previously: 1 black (g) + 0 black (p or u) = 1 black.
    - Now: 0 black (g) + 1 black (p or u) = 1 black.
  - So the number of black nodes on every path through g is unchanged.
  - The only possible new issue is that g (now red) may conflict with its parent; we continue upward.

3. Uncle is black: rotation cases
- Now g is black, p is red, u is black (or null).
- We use rotations to move the red node down and restore the pattern.
- There are two structural cases, depending on whether p is g’s left or right child and whether x is p’s left or right child.

3a. Left-left case (p is g’s left child, x is p’s left child)
